source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

37093.t:
Hoke County swung hard toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race. Cooper beat Whatley here 10,390 to 5,108, a 33-point margin, up from Harris's 6-point edge in 2024. That 27-point move ranks fourth among North Carolina's 100 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county moved 20 points, and the state as a whole moved 23.

Turnout was about 70% of the 2024 vote, 15,939 ballots against 22,724, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Counties with a similar 2024 result moved less: Watauga by 22 points, Pitt by 19 and Washington by 15.

37085.t:
Harnett County flipped in the U.S. Senate race, giving Democrat Cooper a narrow edge over Republican Whatley, 22,011 votes to 21,748, a margin of about 1 point. Trump carried it by 25 points in 2024, so the county moved 26 points toward the Democrats. That was the ninth-largest move among North Carolina's 100 counties, all of which moved left (typical move 20 points; statewide 23).

About 44,986 votes were cast, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among counties with similar 2024 results, Haywood moved almost identically and also flipped, Gaston landed at an even split, and Brunswick moved less, staying Republican by 6 points.

37041.t:
Chowan County moved toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race between Roy Cooper and Michael Whatley, but by less than any other county in North Carolina. Trump carried it by 23 points in 2024; Whatley won it by 11, 3,240 votes to Cooper's 2,578. That 11-point shift ranks 100th of 100 in a state where every county moved left, the typical one by 20 points, and it trails the national typical move of 14. Similar counties moved further: Gates by 18 points, Swain by 23, and Madison by 27, enough to flip it to Cooper.

About 5,928 votes were cast, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

37161.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Rutherford County voted for Whatley over Cooper by 28 points, 14,320 to 8,011. That is 20 points more Democratic than its 48-point margin for Trump in 2024. The shift matches the typical move among North Carolina's 100 counties, all of which moved left, and ranks 51st. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points. Counties of similar size and 2024 vote moved by comparable amounts: Davie by 21 points, McDowell by 23 and Currituck by 15.

Only 22,911 votes were cast, 66% of the 2024 total. With a drop that large, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

37103.t:
Jones County moved toward the Democrats in North Carolina's U.S. Senate race, but by less than most of the state. Trump carried it by 26 points in 2024; this time Whatley won it by 12 over Cooper, 2,140 votes to 1,677, a 14-point shift. That ranks 92nd of the state's 100 counties, all of which moved left, with the typical one moving 20 points. Statewide, Cooper won by 20 in a state Trump carried by 3. Jones's move roughly matches the national typical shift of 14 points but trails similar counties nearby, including Swain (23), Polk (20) and Gates (18).

Turnout was 72% of the 2024 vote, 3,925 ballots against 5,458, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

37031.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Carteret County backed Whatley over Cooper by 28 points, 22,019 votes to 12,166. That is a 15-point swing toward the Democrats from Trump's 43-point win over Harris in 2024. But it is a smaller swing than in most of North Carolina, where every county moved left, the typical one by 20 points. Carteret ranks 89th of 100. Counties with similar 2024 margins and size moved further: Burke and Ashe each shifted 23 points and Lincoln 20.

About 35,142 votes were cast, 77% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

37087.t:

That beat the typical North Carolina county's 20-point shift and ranked 10th of 100 in the state, where every county moved left and 21 flipped from Trump to the Democrat.

About 28,262 votes were cast, roughly 75% of the 2024 total of 37,724, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Harnett, which had the same 2024 margin, ended almost identically. Robeson moved slightly more but stayed narrowly Republican.

It moved further than similar counties Lenoir (16), Martin (17) and Pasquotank (18). It is one of 21 counties in the state that flipped from Trump to the Democrat.

Only 10,386 votes were cast, 71% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Similar counties moved more: Robeson by 27 points, Harnett by 26 and Sampson by 24.

Similar counties moved further, with McDowell at 23 points, Davie at 21 and Rutherford at 20. 37063.t:

Durham ranks 94th of 100 counties, below the typical county's 20 points, and trails similar Democratic counties such as Orange (17), Mecklenburg (21) and Buncombe (21).

Turnout fell to 150,482 votes, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Durham was already the state's most Democratic of these counties, leaving less room to move.

37135.t:

Among similar counties, Durham moved 14 points, while Mecklenburg and Buncombe each moved 21. About 72,153 votes were cast, 83% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Turnout was 439,955 votes, or 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Comparable Democratic-leaning counties moved by similar amounts: Wake by 22 points, Buncombe by 21 and Guilford by 20.

37183.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Wake County voted for Democrat Cooper over Republican Whatley by 47 points, 380,365 to 132,965. That is 22 points more Democratic than its 26-point margin for Harris in 2024. Wake cast more votes than any other North Carolina county, and its swing was close to the statewide move of 23 points and the typical county's 20. It ranked 36th of 100, and every county in the state moved left. Comparable counties shifted almost identically: Buncombe and Mecklenburg by 21 points, Guilford by 20.

Wake cast 523,237 votes, 80% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

37177.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Tyrrell County stayed Republican but by much less: Whatley beat Cooper 690 to 613, a margin of about 6 points, after Trump carried it by about 22 in 2024. That 16-point move toward the Democrats was smaller than the typical North Carolina county's 20 and the state's 23, ranking 83rd of 100. Tyrrell cast the fewest votes in the state, 1,355, with 99% of the expected vote counted.

Turnout was 77% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar small counties moved by comparable amounts: Hyde shifted 16 points and Gates 18, while Chowan moved 11.

37033.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Caswell County stayed Republican but by far less than in 2024. Whatley beat Cooper 4,503 to 4,004, a margin of about 6 points, after Trump carried the county by 25. That is a swing of 19 points toward the Democrats, slightly smaller than the typical North Carolina county's 20-point move. Every county in the state moved left, and Caswell ranks 63rd of 100. Among similar counties, Polk moved 20 points and Swain 23, while Madison moved 27 and flipped to Cooper.

Turnout was well down. The 8,706 votes cast are 72% of the 12,025 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

37023.t:
Burke County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by far less than in 2024. Whatley beat Cooper 17,401 to 11,987, an 18-point margin, after Trump carried the county by 41 points. That 23-point swing toward the Democrats outpaced the typical North Carolina county (20 points), ranking 19th of 100, and topped the national typical move of 14. Similar Trump-leaning counties moved less or about the same: Carteret 15, Lincoln 20, Macon 21.

Only 30,118 votes were cast, 66% of the 2024 total of 45,733, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

37061.t: Duplin County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by far less than in 2024. Whatley carried it 8,718 to 6,933 over Cooper, a margin of 11 points, down from Trump's 29-point win. That 18-point swing toward the Democrats trails both the typical North Carolina county (20 points) and the statewide swing (23), though it beats the national typical move of 14. Among similar counties, Duplin moved more than Beaufort (15) but less than Sampson (24) or Robeson (27). About 16,034 votes were cast, roughly 70% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who simply stayed home.
